messages:
Jamie: FYI we saw a ~15% request fail spike during a spot reclaim in us-west-2 last night. It looks like our drain timing + streaming cutover created a small avalanche where clients retried and overwhelmed on-prem fallback pool.
Sara: Ugh. Any traces that show where the backlog piled up?
Jamie: Traces show many streams got cut mid-token, then clients retried to hosted pool which saturated a single AZ. The token-bridge fallback (our current hack) only handles new sessions, not in-flight streaming.
Mike: Did we have graceful drain timeout long enough for typical streaming sessions? IIRC it's 20s now.
Jamie: 20s. Median active stream remaining length ~45s for a subset of requests (interactive agents). So we often kill mid-stream.
Lee: Two immediate ideas: 1) staggered SLO-aware drain — honor longer grace for connections flagged as "long-lived" or high-priority; 2) support incremental streaming cutover so an in-flight stream can be proxied to a compatible instance instead of being dropped.
Sara: Staggered drains sound doable: mark pods with labels at request admission (eg session-type=streaming, expected-duration=60s) and use that in eviction-controller to prolong pod cordon for those sessions by X seconds. But that delays node reclaim. Cost tradeoff.
Mike: For the proxy hop approach, we could leverage our edge proxy to hold stream state and forward tokens to a new worker. That requires token streaming checkpointing on KV cache and ability to rehydrate on move. Risky but graceful.
Lee: Sketch of a low-risk incremental approach: for preemptible evictions, do a three-step handoff: 1) signal client via header that a cutover is imminent (grace window), 2) snapshot last N tokens/kv and push to ephemeral handoff store, 3) start proxying new requests and allow clients to reconnect and continue from snapshot.
Jamie: Pseudocode we discussed earlier:
```
# eviction hook
cordon(node)
for pod in draining_pods:
  if pod.labels.session-type == "streaming":
    extend_grace(pod, 60)
    snapshot_kv(pod.session_id, last_kv)
    publish_handoff(pod.session_id, last_kv)
  else:
    standard_drain(pod)
```
Sara: Need to be careful: snapshotting KV frequently -> IO + cost. Maybe snapshot only on eviction and keep incremental deltas in-memory with TTL. Also need encryption for handoff store (KMS/HSM).
Mike: Also consider per-request priority routing: for short autoreplies we accept best-effort on spot; for high-SLO streams we pin to dedicated pool or at least route via mixed-capacity pool that prefers non-preemptible instances. That avoids frequent cutovers for the critical path.
Lee: Operationally we should implement metrics + alerting: percent of streams resumed after handoff, percent of streams dropped mid-token, and effective extra reclaim delay caused by extended drains.
k8s-bot: Pod myapp-6789 is now Cordoned (reason=spot-eviction, grace_ext=60s) :information_source:
Sara: Rollout plan proposal: stage 1: add labels/admission hint to mark streaming vs short RPCs; stage 2: implement staggered drain controller that extends grace only for labeled pods + basic snapshot-on-evict to S3-compatible handoff store; stage 3: build edge reconnect path to resume from handoff; stage 4: measure and decide whether to move some traffic classes to dedicated pool.
Jamie: Timeline: 2 weeks for stages 1-2 POC, 4-6 weeks for full reconnect plumbing. Owners: Sara (drain controller), Lee (handoff format + reconnect protocol), Mike (routing + capacity policy).
Mike: Also propose a simple fallback: if handoff fails, mark request as high retryable and queue to reorder against rate limits so it doesn't spike host pool. That buys us safety.
Sara: I'll draft a short runbook for oncall: how to increase drain time, how to toggle handoff (feature flag), and emergency rollback.
Lee: Also need to update capacity estimator to account for longer average pod lifetime during mass evictions — else autoscaler will undershoot.
Jamie: OK sounds actionable. Sara/Lee/Mike please post PR for controller + small sim harness so we can run chaos tests. :thumbsup:
Sara: Will do. I'll open the PR and assign reviewers.
Mike: I'll add a routing feature-flag and a small canary to test mixed pools.
Lee: I'll start work on the handoff proto and small reconnect client lib.
Jamie: Thanks all. Follow-ups in next infra sync.
